name: FORGE

intro.problem: A trained model reports a confidence but not whether that confidence is earned, so a researcher cannot tell whether a model has learned all it can or has simply run out of data.
intro.value: Splitting predictive uncertainty into a reducible part and an irreducible part tells a researcher when more data or better features would help and when the model has reached its limit.
intro.approach: We decompose predictive variance with the law of total variance, compute it with a fast Laplace approximation checked against Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and present it on a web dashboard across three reproductions: music-genre classification, phonon density-of-states regression, and long-lived-particle detection.
intro.goals: The capstone delivered the observatory and its metrics; what remains is to answer the open questions it raised and carry its lessons back into the live analysis work, toward a platform where researchers load their own models.

questions: Is a model's confidence earned, or has it run out of data?
When does a fast posterior approximation agree with the gold-standard sampler, and when does it not?
Can the same uncertainty measures be compared across classification and regression models?

open.text: Does a training penalty that is not a likelihood, such as a decorrelation or closure term, belong in the posterior's curvature?
When two networks share one label, should the joint posterior use a sandwich correction or be declared a Gibbs measure over the training objective?
What is the posterior on the background estimate itself, propagated through both networks and the region cuts?
Should epistemic variance be reported in logit space or probability space when the two disagree?
The fast Laplace path over-states epistemic variance against the sampler on every board tested; no correction has been applied.
Rank-based input scaling rescued heavy-tailed features that min-max scaling silently flattened; not yet carried into the current analysis line.
Selecting checkpoints on the fold being graded biases the reported metric; the current trainers have not been audited for it.
The public site serves only the splash; the dashboard is built but not wired in behind it.

timeline.label: Capstone opens: Bayesian posterior observatory proposed
